pages.text: The command panel: a map, 4 repeaters, 4 comparators. Hold it and press the command key: a camera from above.

WASD moves, the wheel lifts, Q and E turn. Left click selects, right click orders. Ctrl+digit makes a group, F2 selects the army. The card uses SC2 hotkeys: M move, S stop, H hold, P patrol, A attack; workers build with B and V, then a left click puts the building, Esc or a right click cancels.

Workers: G and a click mine that block; G and a drag mine the whole area (up to 32 by 32) — minerals first — until it is empty. Selected workers show their area and the block they mine. A and a click on any creature — a monster, an animal — attacks it. As in SC2, some weapons hit only the air (a flying viking, corruptor, phoenix) or only the ground (a tank, a colossus, a banshee).

The camera goes anywhere — keys, screen edges, a click on the minimap — however far you stand: the world round it is loaded for you. A cyan arrow on the minimap is you, pointing where you look.$(br2)$(l)F4$() or the ☺ button selects YOU as a hero: you carry out move, stop, hold, patrol and attack orders yourself, striking with what is in your right hand. The card then shows your hotbar: click an item to take it in hand, again to use it. The command panel used on one of your units takes control of it.

The $(l)middle button$() held and dragged pans the view; held on the $(l)minimap$() it drags the map itself. Terran barracks, factories, starports and command centers $(l)lift off$() (L), fly where they are sent and land again (L). Units that change form — siege mode, burrow, phasing, defender mode, a hellion into a hellbat — play their $(l)morph$() and look different after; the AI uses every ability its units have.

$(l)Tunnels and caves:$() the four buttons at the top left cut the land away — ▼ and ▲ lower and raise a level above which no block is drawn, + and - a radius round the camera — so an army underground is seen and commanded; all off by default. Your units hidden from the camera show as framed icons. $(l)Aircraft$() fly higher or lower with the card's Higher and Lower buttons, down to a block over the ground: into a cave's mouth or a tunnel.$(br2)Sent where they cannot walk, ground armies wait while workers cut them a tunnel, stairs or a bridge — in ordinary worlds; on a StarCraft II battle map the map's relief stays as it is.

$(l)Autocast$(): right-click an ability's button on the command card and the units cast it themselves when it fits (a gold frame turns round the button); right-click again to stop. The zealot's charge is on from the start, as in StarCraft II. A worker's $(l)Gather$() button does the same for seeking resources by itself.
